title: Camera follow + closer framing — damped pursuit of local bomber, ~10-12 tile view size (vs current whole-arena fit)
intent: User feedback 2026-05-28: 'камера всегда както далеко от арены'. Current camera (per visual-style.md §7.1) is LOCKED at arena centre + sized to fit the whole arena. With recent arena variants (corridor 21×7, cross 17×17, wide 17×13) the camera is pulled back so far that bombers + bombs read small. Per visual-style.md §7.2 target — orthographic + damped follow + 12-18 tile view — was intended for MVP-3 chunked maps. Pulling that target FORWARD: now is the right time. This story implements a damped camera follow that tracks the local player (or arena centre in spectator / bot-vs-bot modes), with a view size of ~10-12 tiles across (closer than today's whole-arena fit). Edge-clamping prevents the camera from sliding past arena bounds. Per-tab in multiplayer (each client follows its own local bomber).
rationale: Source: user feedback 2026-05-28 + visual-style.md §7.2 (the camera-follow target was always planned for chunked-arena era; pulling forward is justified because the new arena variants from S140+S143 already need it). Closer framing also improves: pickup recognition (icons more legible), bomber-personality visual reads (palette/accessories more visible), shadow/light interactions from GDP-2026-05-28-001 (closer = more apparent). Cheap to ship — ~80 LOC camera-follow system + the existing CameraWaypoint primitive may already cover most of the surface.
acceptanceHints: Reference: `docs/game-design/visual-style.md §7.2` (Target camera shape) — this story implements that target now instead of deferring.
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/camera-follow-system.ts: NEW.
Query for the LOCAL bomber (PlayerControlled component on the bomber entity).
Per renderUpdate (not fixedUpdate — camera is presentation):
1. Compute target camera world position = bomber Transform.position + cameraOffset (default: bomber height + ~10 cells up + ~7 cells back-of-camera, calibrated to give a ~60° pitch view).
2. Damp current camera position toward target via lerp(cur, target, 0.12 × dt × 60) — feels stable, not jittery, ~0.15s to settle.

3. Edge clamp: if the damped target would push the camera's view-frustum past the arena's hard bounds (so the player sees out-of-arena empty space) → clamp the camera laterally so view stays within bounds.
4. Apply camera lookAt = (bomber position + small look-ahead offset toward facing direction × 0.5 cells).
VIEW SIZE TUNING:
Target: ~11 tiles visible across the wider screen dimension (was ~15-17 to fit whole-arena).

Approach 1 — perspective: keep PerspectiveCamera; reduce FOV from current ~50° to ~40° AND move camera closer (height + back-of-camera offset). Calibrate to ~11-tile horizontal coverage at typical 16:9 aspect ratio.
Approach 2 — orthographic: switch to OrthographicCamera with view-size = 11 tiles × cell-size. Grid-distance constant across screen — preferred per visual-style.md §7.2 prose.

Recommended: approach 2 (orthographic). Better for grid readability + simpler edge-clamp math. If renderer doesn't yet support orthographic (per `dynabomber-readiness-analysis.md §1` historical gap), perspective fallback works as v1.
EDGE CLAMPING:

Compute the rectangle the camera 'sees' at floor height (project the view frustum to Y=0). If the rectangle's left edge would be < arena's left bound: shift camera right so left edge aligns with arena left bound. Same logic right / top / bottom.

Result: on small arenas (15×11 default, 13×11 plaza) the camera mostly STAYS centred because the whole arena fits within ~11 tiles. On large arenas (21×7 corridor, 17×17 cross) the camera ACTUALLY follows the bomber.
Edge-clamp behaviour also kicks in when the bomber is near the arena edge — camera stops sliding so player sees a 'wall' of the arena rather than past it.
LOOK-AHEAD:
Small (~0.5 cells) lookAt offset toward the bomber's GridMover facing direction. Gives the player slightly more 'forward visibility' in the direction they're moving.
Disable look-ahead when bomber is standing still (no facing change → no offset).
Per visual-style.md §7.3 'no aggressive look-ahead; cap so bombs behind the bomber stay visible'. 0.5 cells is gentle enough.
MULTIPLE BOMBERS (multi-bot solo, multiplayer):
Solo mode: camera follows player.1 ONLY (PlayerControlled tag). Bots are followed by their own client in connected mode; in solo mode bots are visible as remote scene objects.
Multiplayer connected: each tab's camera follows ITS OWN local player (via the existing 'is this my Presence?' check from S109 remote-bomber-decorator).
Bot-vs-bot regression test: no PlayerControlled entity exists. Camera falls back to arena-centre (current behaviour preserved as a feature-flag mode).
DEAD BOMBER:

When local bomber dies (BomberStats.alive=false) → camera HOLDS at last-living position for 0.6s (matching ragdoll duration). After bomber despawn, camera transitions to next-living-player view (in multiplayer) OR arena centre (in solo).
Spectator mode (mid-round join from GDP-022-012): camera follows arena centre by default; player can press [1] / [2] / [3] / [4] to follow a specific bomber.
Round-resolve banner moment: camera holds at last-living-player position for the 3-second auto-restart window. Don't snap-cut.
URL CONFIGURATION:
`?camera=follow` (default) — current local player followed.
`?camera=centre` — locked to arena centre (current behaviour). Useful for screenshot tests, bot-vs-bot watching.
`?camera=follow&viewSize=N` — override view size to N tiles wide (range 8..20, default 11).
`?camera=spectate-bomber.X` — follow a specific bomber entity by ID. Useful for spectator playtests.
RECORDING / REPLAY:

Recordings already capture all relevant gameplay state. Camera-follow is RECONSTRUCTED at replay time, not stored as part of the recording (camera = presentation per `gameplay-systems.md §9.1`). Existing `recordings/demo-30s.recording.json` still replays correctly with new camera.
DETERMINISM: camera is pure presentation. Bot-vs-bot regression unaffected. Visual replay differs per camera-config but gameplay state is identical.
PERFORMANCE: one camera Transform update per frame. Negligible.
DOCS UPDATES IN THIS PR:
visual-style.md §7.1 → mark as legacy 'pre-2026-05-28 camera was arena-centre + whole-arena fit'.
visual-style.md §7.2 → 'shipped 2026-05-28' marker; describes current state.
ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST:
Default load → camera framed close enough that bomber + ~10 surrounding cells are clearly visible. Bomber + power-up icons + bomb mesh all legible.
Walk to arena edge → camera slows / stops sliding (edge clamp); player sees a stable view of the arena edge.
Cross arena 17×17 → camera follows player through quadrants; doesn't try to fit the whole arena.
Default arena 15×11 → camera mostly stays centred (whole arena fits in the ~11-tile view); only edge-snap when bomber is at extreme corners.
Multiplayer: 2 tabs see different camera positions, each centred on its own bomber. Both see each other when bombers are close.
Dead bomber: camera holds for 0.6s then transitions cleanly.
`?camera=centre` URL → reverts to whole-arena fixed view.
UNIT TESTS:
Camera target position = bomber pos + offset, every renderUpdate.
Damping: target jumps 10 cells → camera settles within 0.15s.
Edge clamp: bomber at arena left edge → camera doesn't slide past left bound.
Spectator fallback: no PlayerControlled in scene → camera at arena centre.
?camera=centre URL → follow system disabled, camera locked.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Free-camera mode (player rotates / pans). Locked yaw + locked pitch per visual-style.md §7.
Cinematic camera moves (intro pan, victory zoom-in). The existing round-resolve zoom-in from visual-style.md §7.4 stays as a separate consideration.
Multi-target framing (camera that frames ALL bombers simultaneously). Single-target follow.
Screen shake on player damage (visual-style.md §6.3 explicit ban remains).
Camera collision avoidance (camera can clip through walls — that's fine for top-down view).
Per-arena custom camera presets. One camera config used across all arenas (edge clamp + damped follow handles arena-size differences gracefully).
